names.details: FAṢL MEMLEKET-İ EFRENC VE ERMEN VE NAṢĀRĀ BEYĀNI VE ḪULEFĀ-YI MESĪḤ İ‘LĀNI ẔİKRİNDEDÜR (Section: Description of the Lands of the Franks, Armenians, and Christians, and Mention of the Successors of the Messiah): Let it not remain hidden that the ḥudūd-ı vilāyet-i Ermen (boundaries of the Armenian province) form a vast land opposite Gürcistān (Georgia).Its capital districts are Ermeniyye-i Ṣuġrā (Armenia Minor) and Ermeniyye-i Kübrā (Greater Armenia).The length (ṭūl) of Ermeniyye-i Kübrā stretches from the frontier of Āzerbaycān (Azerbaijan) to the boundary of Selmās (Salmas, Iran).Its breadth (‘arż) extends from the beginning of the Gürcistān (Georgia) province to the farthest limit of Vesṭān. As for Ermeniyye-i Ṣuġrā (Armenia Minor), its length reaches from the Syrian side (Şām ṭarafı) to the extreme frontier of the vilāyet-i Rūm (Anatolia). Likewise, its breadth runs from the frontier of Malāṭiyye (Malatya) to the border of Anṭākiyye (Antioch). All directions, regions, and mountains are included within this territory. In ancient times, there were five inhabited principal towns, which were called: Ayās (Yumurtalık, Turkey), Sīs (Kozan, Turkey), Ṭarsūs (Tarsus, Turkey), Adana (Adana, Turkey), and Misīs (Misis / Yakapınar, Turkey). All of them lie near one another. In our time, the largest of these towns is Adana. Misīs and Ayās are in ruins, while Sīs and Ṭarsūs have become towns of medium size. In former days, the region had twenty thousand inhabited villages and fertile settlements; it is reported that today no tithe (‘öşr) remains from them. Among its products: ṣūf (woollen cloth), called ḳudsī, is said to be woven in Anḳara (Ankara), which is subject to the vilāyet-i Rūm. And lāden (labdanum; fragrant resin), renowned for its delightful scent, is produced on the nearby Cezīre-i Ḳıbrıs (the Island of Cyprus). [translation]
